notes: Howbeit goes to οὖν and μέν stands unrepresented, which is rule 70 in terms: μέν is joined neither to the answering connective nor to a preceding οὖν, which keeps its own word. Giving Howbeit to μέν instead remains defensible.
ὁ → he is rule 32's substantival article before a participle, supplying the pronoun and nothing else.
A reference comparison will report the unrepresented μέν as a disagreement; rule 70 says that report is not a correction.
